label: early copy phase (first copy step), boosted on inputs d/f/a/b
explanation: Broad copy-phase feature (79% of activation mass in the copy phase). The strongest single locus is the first copy step (recall_idx==1, input = orig(0) right after <DEL>), with a 42% firing rate and 40% of mass, and the top activations are all there. It also fires at recall_idx 2, with a weaker tail on the delimiter and the late original-phase steps of long sequences, rising with L. Within the copy phase it fires more on certain input tokens (d 3.8x, f, a, b, q) and output tokens (d, h, i, m); sequences starting with d are especially strong. It is almost silent on early original-phase steps (t<=3). Magnitude is highest at recall_idx 1 and when orig(0) is d/a/f/i. Token selectivity is graded, not crisp, so precision stays around 0.43 and dev F1 around 0.49.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: d, b, f, a; input phase: f, q, a, e; delimiter step: ) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: d, u, i, h; copy phase: d, h, i, m; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=10, L=9 & t=10.
